data.narrative:
Newspace Research is a Series B defense and security company that has raised $73.2M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 10 peers: 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms at the same stage. The private peer set spans valuations from $300M to $3.0B, with a median of $1.1B; named comps include Dream Security ($3.0B), Allen Control Systems ($2.2B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Code Metal ($1.2B), and Twenty ($1.0B).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x multiplier to the $73M raised proxy, implying a $139M valuation consistent with typical Series B advancement dynamics. Peer-median analysis, drawing on the 8 same-sector, same-stage private comps, implies $1.1B based on the median valuation across the cohort.

These methods produce a triangulated range of $118M (low) to $1.3B (high), with a median of $632M. The wide dispersion reflects material heterogeneity within the defense/security peer set—a $10x spread from floor to ceiling—and raises questions about which peer segments are most comparable. Key uncertainties include revenue multiples, customer concentration, and growth rates among the comps, none of which are present in this dataset. The stage-progression method likely understates value given the elevated valuations in the peer cohort; however, without revenue or profitability data, anchoring precision remains limited.
